security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode code uses CSRRS or CSRRC (including pseudo-instructions) on pmpaddr CSRs to modify a subset of bits, causing bits that 'read as' a different value (e.g., unimplemented address bits [G-1] and above that read as 0) to be read-modify-written back with their apparent read value, silently corrupting the underlying hardware state of those bits
security_spec.summary: CSRRS/CSRRC on pmpaddr triggers unintended RMW of 'reads-as' shadow bits, corrupting PMP underlying state and weakening M-mode memory isolation enforced by OpenSBI

findings.finding: PMP address value is computed entirely in local variables (CPU registers) then written via csr_write_num(pmpaddr_csr, pmpaddr) which expands to CSRW — a pure write instruction. No CSRRS/CSRRC touches pmpaddr CSRs, so unimplemented upper address bits that 'read as 0' are never read-modify-written back.
All CSR_PMPADDR0 through CSR_PMPADDR63 writes are dispatched via csr_write() which emits the CSRW instruction. No CSRRS/CSRRC is used for any pmpaddr CSR.
pmp_disable() only reads-modifies-writes pmpcfg CSRs (clearing the A field) and never touches pmpaddr CSRs at all. No risk of pmpaddr corruption.
All CSR_PMPADDR0 through CSR_PMPADDR63 reads use csr_read() which emits the CSRR instruction. Pure read, no writeback regardless of what 'reads as' bits return.
SMEPMP configuration calls pmp_set() and pmp_disable() exclusively. The csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, ...) touches MSECCFG (not pmpaddr) and is unrelated to this vulnerability pattern.
csr_set() emits the CSRS instruction. Verified across the entire codebase: it is never called with a pmpaddr CSR number. All call sites use it on MSECCFG only.
MIPS platform PMP override only touches MIPS-specific PMACFG CSRs (cacheability attributes), not standard pmpaddr CSRs. Uses safe read-modify-write pattern via local variable on pmacfg.
